requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The active pwquality configuration sets minlen=12. An 11-character password was directly rejected for being shorter than 12, while a valid 12-character, three-class password was accepted both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes.
requirements.summary: The active configuration sets minclass=3. A 22-character password containing only two classes was rejected specifically for having fewer than three classes, while a 12-character password with three classes was accepted after restart. Both PAM password stacks reference pam_pwquality.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation used the installed libpwquality and PAM components. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were unchanged after execution and restart, with package health remaining clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct policy and behavioral checks demonstrate the required minimum length and character-class rules, including after a verified restart. The restart protocol is complete: node1 was healthy before restart, the restart was acknowledged, its boot ID changed from 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72 to d8c3a946-8230-42e8-a036-ac103c863594, and the system, PAM configuration, policy, password behavior, SSH listener, and package health recovered. Fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot transition and platform preservation.
limitations: Password behavior was tested directly through pwscore with PAM hook inspection rather than through an end-to-end password change for a test user; the evidence is nevertheless coherent and directly exercises the configured libpwquality rules.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The policy-file creation and permission setting directly implemented the task (cmd-4aac6441c8664185); the transient scheduled reboot fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-4006290d0aff465c); and bounded temporary evidence files were removed by the same final verification command (cmd-46ed8e6e4a6b45c6). The failed post-restart OpenSSL-based probe did not show a managed-state mutation and was corrected using available tooling. Final snapshots show no failed services, new exposure, package damage, or executor residue.
